description: The object-detection model_type vocabulary this engine accepts. A training run's model_type arrives in experiment_parameters and is resolved by core.utils.object_detection_utils.resolve_family; anything outside accepted_model_type_values raises ValueError before training starts. Published so a producer (the model-zoo's per-file model_type declaration, the backend's MODEL_TYPE_CHOICES, the SDK) can assert in its own CI that what it emits this engine can actually route, instead of the two sides discovering a disagreement when a user's experiment fails (backend#1829).

families.notes: The torchvision detection-API contract (model returns a loss dict in train mode). 'rcnn' is a legacy alias kept for already-deployed experiments and is the value the backend actually stores today.
Grid-tensor output + external loss, fixed 448 input. The family name equals the declared value, so it needs no alias.

DETR / RT-DETR / D-FINE / OWLv2 / Grounding DINO speak this contract. Registered but NOT wired: every entry point raises NotImplementedError with an actionable message, deliberately, rather than mis-running on the torchvision path. training_supported=false is therefore a fact about this engine, not a placeholder — a producer that emits this value gets a clear refusal, which is the intended behaviour until the transformer path lands.

not_accepted.description: Architecture-level names are NOT accepted — a producer declares the FAMILY, not the architecture. Listed explicitly because the model-zoo ships files declaring these strings today (backend#1829), so a consumer's check must treat them as failures rather than assume they resolve.

matching.empty_or_absent: Defaulted upstream by use_cases/object_detection/main.py::_infer_model_type (to the rcnn family, or yolo when the model id / class name contains 'yolo') before it ever reaches resolve_family. An empty value is therefore NOT rejected — only an explicit unrecognised one is.
